events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 6 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. * WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa Coastal Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Tuesday to midnight CST Thursday night. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM CST Tuesday through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 16 at 6:56PM CST until November 20 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
6 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa
Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Tuesday to
midnight CST Thursday night. For the High Rip Current Risk,
from 6 AM CST Tuesday through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...As widespread snowfall has dissipated this evening, the Winter Weather Advisory will be allowed to expire. Some lingering light snow showers may continue for the next hour or two. For the Winter Storm Warning, heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 1 to 3 feet above 5000 feet, with up to 4 feet at the highest peaks. Total snow accumulations up to a foot between 4000 and 5000 feet. Light flurries to a dusting is possible as low as 3500 feet. Winds gusting as high as 55 mph. * WHERE...For the Winter Storm Warning, elevations above 4000 feet in the Sierra Nevada and southern Cascades. * WHEN...From 10 PM Tuesday to 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Snow covered roads, travel delays, and chain controls will continue to be possible through this afternoon and evening impacting the evening commute. Travel could be very difficult to impossible Tuesday night through early Friday morning. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches and significant reductions in visibilities. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Lull in activity expected on Tuesday, followed by a colder, stronger system by mid-week. Snow levels 3500-4500 feet Tuesday night, rising to around 4500-5500 feet Wednesday. Heaviest snow is expected Wednesday morning into the afternoon, with snowfall rates 1-2+ inches per hour.

weather.instruction:

cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.instruction:

dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, SW Kenai Peninsula, NW Kenai Peninsula, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Power outages and tree damage are likely due to the ice. Travel could be nearly impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

location.region: Anchorage; Anchorage Hillside / Eagle River; Lower Matanuska Valley; SW Kenai Peninsula; NW Kenai Peninsula; Interior Kenai Peninsula; Turnagain Pass

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-19 feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the secondary high tide in the evening.

location.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

weather.description:

feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from
late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and
harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to
Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean
drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea.
Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches
and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood
advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the
secondary high tide in the evening.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Mixed precipitation in Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, and NW Kenai Peninsula; heavy snowfall for Interior Kenai Peninsula and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This product was updated to remove SW Kenai Peninsula and correct impact information in the bullet above. An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12 to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored breakpoints along the coast from this afternoon through Friday morning. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 18 at 1:25AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored break points. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

weather.description:

weather.instruction:

dangerous surf conditions.

float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10- 18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.

expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous
rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
moderate coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is
likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially
to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for
ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out
to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore.
Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through
the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous
surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.

NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Pooling of sea
water is possible around high tide at beach and harbor areas
that is uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach
erosion is also possible. No significant damage is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may occur near
early morning high tide. Additional hazardous surf and coastal
flooding issues are expected next week.
weather.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.
weather.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST this evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 3:43AM CST until November 20 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 6 feet
in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST this evening. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.2 ft of
inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM PST Friday.
For the High Surf Advisory until 1 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high
tide is expected to be 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at
7:15 AM Thursday and 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45
AM Friday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents and rough surf.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.instruction:

inside as carbon monoxide poisoning can result.

Check with your local, city, or county officials for information on
available warming centers.

Be sure to dress in layers if outdoors. Make sure that pets and
livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler, Eastern Clay, Eastern Putnam, Inland Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns, Northern Inland St. Johns, South Central Duval, Southeast Coastal St. Johns, Southern Inland St. Johns, Trout River, Western Clay, Western Duval, Western Putnam and Western St. Johns. * WHEN...Through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Several rounds of heavy rainfall are expected to repeatedly occur in the watch area through at least early Friday evening. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall will result in the potential for urban and small stream flooding across portions of northeast and north central Florida. Widespread rainfall totals of 3 to 6 inches are forecast, with locally higher amounts up to 12 inches possible. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor flooding around
times of high tide. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 8 to 11 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous
rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM EST Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: Flood Watch issued November 16 at 3:18PM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole,
Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie,
and Martin counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast
through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast
with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest
potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal
counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by upstream dam release continues. * WHERE...Maricopa County in south central Arizona... Northeastern Yuma County in southwestern Arizona... * WHEN...Until 1100 AM MST Tuesday Nov 24. * IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 815 AM MST, water releases from Painted Rock Dam continue with flow peaking around 3000 cfs. A streamflow gauge immediately downstream also indicated a stage near 10 feet. - Flooding is expected along the Gila River. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED 05:30 PST Thu Nov 19 2026 The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING for the following areas: NWS Reno NV - NVZ002 (Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA)) * WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger exists in the backcountry. Large avalanches are expected across backcountry terrain. * WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy 49) on the north and Ebbetts Pass (Hwy 4) on the south, including the greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to backcountry areas, not to ski areas and highways where avalanche mitigation programs exist. * WHEN...In effect from Thu 05:30 PST to Fri 04:00 PST. * IMPACTS...Significant amounts of new snow and wind are creating dangerous avalanche conditions in the backcountry. The new snow is overloading a weak snowpack in some upper elevation areas. Avalanches could run down into treed terrain. * PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche conditions exist in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below backcountry avalanche terrain is not recommended during HIGH avalanche danger. Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or www.avalanche.org for more detailed information. Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage area of this or any avalanche center.

events.title: Winter Storm Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow Above 5,000 feet. Additional snow accumulations 3 to 8 inches above 5,000 feet; 1 to 3 feet above 7,000 feet. Winds gusting as high as 50 mph along the Sierra Crest. * WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet. * WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.

location.region: Yosemite NP outside of the valley; San Joaquin River Canyon; Upper San Joaquin River; Kaiser to Rodgers Ridge; Kings Canyon NP; Grant Grove Area; Sequoia NP; South End of the Upper Sierra

weather.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 19 at 4:46PM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow Above 5,000 feet. Additional snow accumulations 3
to 8 inches above 5,000 feet; 1 to 3 feet above 7,000 feet. Winds
gusting as high as 50 mph along the Sierra Crest.

* WHERE...Sierra Nevada above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.
weather.areaDesc: Yosemite NP outside of the valley; San Joaquin River Canyon; Upper San Joaquin River; Kaiser to Rodgers Ridge; Kings Canyon NP; Grant Grove Area; Sequoia NP; South End of the Upper Sierra

events.description: * WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Far South Miami-Dade County, Inland Broward County, Inland Miami-Dade County, Inland Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...Through Friday morning. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1.4 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18 to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored break points. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM PST Saturday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.9 ft MLLW) at 7:45 AM Friday and 1.4 ft above normal (7.2 ft MLLW) at 8:15 AM Saturday. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Pacific Coast will likely be added to the Advisory as early as Sunday with the San Francisco and San Pablo Bays upgraded to a Coastal Flood Warning as we approach "King Tides".

events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... Any additional heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above record flood levels through late week and into this weekend. For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage Fish Camp. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 2:15 AM EST Friday the stage was 18.6 feet. - Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 2:15 AM EST Friday was 18.6 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady within Major Flood Stage, cresting at 18.7 feet. - Flood stage is 16.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Brevard, FL

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 20 at 3:10AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage, well
above its previous record flood stage. Any additional heavy rainfall
over the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above
record flood levels through late week and into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 AM EST Friday the stage was 18.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:15 AM EST Friday was 18.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage, cresting at 18.7 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at noon EST.
weather.areaDesc: Brevard, FL

erosion is expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best

weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of

weather.description:

* WHERE...Interior Monterey County and the Santa Lucia Range, Most of

* IMPACTS...Cold conditions will be hazardous, especially for
vulnerable populations. Prolonged exposure will lead to hypothermia
for people and animals.
weather.instruction:
Ensure portable heaters are working properly and are used correctly
to avoid sparking a fire indoors. Do not use generators or grills
inside as carbon monoxide poisoning can result.

Check with your local, city, or county officials for information on
available warming centers.

Be sure to dress in layers if outdoors. Make sure that pets and
livestock have adequate food, unfrozen water, and warmth. Cover or
tend to sensitive crops, plants, and vegetation.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
5 to 12 feet in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb through Minor Flood Stage at the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to continue climbing through this weekend. Towards late weekend and into early next week, the river is anticipated to reach Major Flood Stage. For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Deland. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 7:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 4.5 feet. - Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 7:30 PM EST Thursday was 4.5 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 5.7 feet early next week. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 4.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 19 at 8:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb through Minor Flood
Stage at the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
continue climbing through this weekend. Towards late weekend and into
early next week, the river is anticipated to reach Major Flood Stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 4.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Thursday was 4.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 5.7 feet early next
week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1100 AM EST.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 19 at 7:38PM CST until November 21 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Mobile AL
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
